body.en: Calculus rests on a single foundational idea: what value does a function approach as its input creeps toward a target? It need not ever reach that target value — what matters is the local trend and the behavior of the function in arbitrarily small deleted neighborhoods.

body.en: Mastering limits begins with understanding the difference between the actual output of a function at a point and the values it approaches from the left and right.

body.en:
We write \( \displaystyle \lim_{x \to c} f(x) = L \) if the outputs \( f(x) \) can be made arbitrarily close to \( L \) by taking \( x \) sufficiently close to \( c \) (with \( x \neq c \)).

  • Left-Hand Limit: \( \displaystyle \lim_{x \to c^-} f(x) = L_1 \) considers only inputs \( x < c \).
  • Right-Hand Limit: \( \displaystyle \lim_{x \to c^+} f(x) = L_2 \) considers only inputs \( x > c \).

label.ar: ● مبرهنة & برهان · Two-Sided النهاية Existence Criterion

body.en:
Theorem: The two-sided limit \( \displaystyle \lim_{x \to c} f(x) = L \) exists and equals \( L \) if and only if both one-sided limits exist and are equal to \( L \): \[ \lim_{x \to c} f(x) = L \iff \lim_{x \to c^-} f(x) = L \quad \text{and} \quad \lim_{x \to c^+} f(x) = L. \]

Proof:
(\(\implies\)) Suppose \( \lim_{x\to c} f(x) = L \). By definition, for every \( \varepsilon > 0 \), there exists \( \delta > 0 \) such that \( 0 < |x - c| < \delta \implies |f(x) - L| < \varepsilon \). For all \( x \in (c - \delta, c) \), we have \( 0 < |x - c| < \delta \), hence \( |f(x) - L| < \varepsilon \), proving \( \lim_{x\to c^-} f(x) = L \). Identical reasoning holds for \( x \in (c, c + \delta) \), proving \( \lim_{x\to c^+} f(x) = L \).
(\(\impliedby\)) Suppose both one-sided limits equal \( L \). Given \( \varepsilon > 0 \), there exist \( \delta_1 > 0 \) such that \( c - \delta_1 < x < c \implies |f(x) - L| < \varepsilon \), and \( \delta_2 > 0 \) such that \( c < x < c + \delta_2 \implies |f(x) - L| < \varepsilon \). Setting \( \delta = \min(\delta_1, \delta_2) > 0 \), it follows that whenever \( 0 < |x - c| < \delta \), either \( x \in (c - \delta, c) \) or \( x \in (c, c + \delta) \); in both cases \( |f(x) - L| < \varepsilon \). Thus \( \lim_{x\to c} f(x) = L \). \( \blacksquare \)
body.ar:
Theorem: The two-sided النهاية \( \displaystyle \lim_{x \to c} f(x) = L \) exists and equals \( L \) if and only if both one-sided النهايات exist and are equal to \( L \): \[ \lim_{x \to c} f(x) = L \iff \lim_{x \to c^-} f(x) = L \quad \text{and} \quad \lim_{x \to c^+} f(x) = L. \]

Proof:
(\(\implies\)) Suppose \( \lim_{x\to c} f(x) = L \). By definition, for every \( \varepsilon > 0 \), there exists \( \delta > 0 \) such that \( 0 < |x - c| < \delta \implies |f(x) - L| < \varepsilon \). For all \( x \in (c - \delta, c) \), we have \( 0 < |x - c| < \delta \), ومنه \( |f(x) - L| < \varepsilon \), proving \( \lim_{x\to c^-} f(x) = L \). Identical reasoning holds for \( x \in (c, c + \delta) \), proving \( \lim_{x\to c^+} f(x) = L \).
(\(\impliedby\)) Suppose both one-sided النهايات equal \( L \). المعطيات \( \varepsilon > 0 \), there exist \( \delta_1 > 0 \) such that \( c - \delta_1 < x < c \implies |f(x) - L| < \varepsilon \), and \( \delta_2 > 0 \) such that \( c < x < c + \delta_2 \implies |f(x) - L| < \varepsilon \). Setting \( \delta = \min(\delta_1, \delta_2) > 0 \), it follows that whenever \( 0 < |x - c| < \delta \), either \( x \in (c - \delta, c) \) or \( x \in (c, c + \delta) \); in both cases \( |f(x) - L| < \varepsilon \). وعليه \( \lim_{x\to c} f(x) = L \). \( \blacksquare \)

body.en:
A function \( f \) is continuous at a point \( x = c \) if and only if all three conditions are satisfied:

  1. \( f(c) \) is defined: \( c \) is in the domain of \( f \).
  2. \( \displaystyle \lim_{x \to c} f(x) \) exists: \( \displaystyle \lim_{x \to c^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to c^+} f(x) = L \), where \( L \) is finite.
  3. \( \displaystyle \lim_{x \to c} f(x) = f(c) \): The limit value equals the function output.
body.ar:
A الدالة \( f \) is continuous at a point \( x = c \) if and only if all three conditions are satisfied:

  1. \( f(c) \) is defined: \( c \) is in the المجال of \( f \).
  2. \( \displaystyle \lim_{x \to c} f(x) \) exists: \( \displaystyle \lim_{x \to c^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to c^+} f(x) = L \), حيث \( L \) is finite.
  3. \( \displaystyle \lim_{x \to c} f(x) = f(c) \): The النهاية value equals the الدالة output.

body.en:
Depending on which conditions of the continuity checklist fail, graphs display one of seven geometric cases:

  • Case 1 · Continuous everywhere at \(c\): All 3 conditions hold without interruption: \(f(c)\) is defined, \(\lim_{x\to c} f(x) = L\) exists, and \(\lim_{x\to c} f(x) = f(c)\).
  • Case 2 · Removable Discontinuity (Hole): Condition 1 fails (\(f(c)\) undefined), while Condition 2 passes (\(\lim_{x\to c} f(x)\) exists).
  • Case 3 · Removable Discontinuity (Displaced Point): Conditions 1 & 2 pass, but Condition 3 fails (\(\lim_{x\to c} f(x) \neq f(c)\)).
  • Case 4 · Jump Discontinuity: Condition 2 fails because one-sided limits are finite but unequal: \(\lim_{x\to c^-} f(x) \neq \lim_{x\to c^+} f(x)\).
  • Case 5 · Infinite Discontinuity (Vertical Asymptote): Condition 2 fails because one or both one-sided limits grow without bound (\(\pm\infty\)).
  • Case 6 · Oscillating Discontinuity: Condition 2 fails because outputs oscillate infinitely many times between bounds (e.g., \(\sin(2/(x-c))\)).
  • Case 7 · One-Sided / Endpoint Continuity: The function is defined on a closed or half-closed interval such as \([a, b]\); the two-sided limit does not exist at boundary point \(c = a\) because values outside \([a, b]\) are undefined, but the one-sided limit matches the endpoint value: \(\lim_{x\to a^+} f(x) = f(a)\).

body.en:
Why Differentiability Implies Continuity & How Implicit Differentiation Works: Notice that for \(x \ne a\), we can write \(f(x) - f(a) = \dfrac{f(x) - f(a)}{x - a}\cdot (x - a)\). Taking the limit as \(x \to a\) by the Product Law gives:

\[ \lim_{x \to a} \bigl(f(x) - f(a)\bigr) = f'(a)\cdot 0 = 0 \implies \lim_{x \to a} f(x) = f(a) \]

Similarly, when differentiating an implicit relation \(F(x, y) = c\) with respect to \(x\), \(y = y(x)\) is an inner function of \(x\). By the Chain Rule, \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\bigl[y^n\bigr] = ny^{n-1}\dfrac{dy}{dx}\), and for product terms \(\dfrac{d}{dx}[xy] = y + x\dfrac{dy}{dx}\).

Why Differentiability Implies Continuity & How Implicit Differentiation Works: Notice that for \(x \ne a\), we can write \(f(x) - f(a) = \dfrac{f(x) - f(a)}{x - a}\cdot (x - a)\). Taking the النهاية as \(x \to a\) by the Product Law gives:

\[ \lim_{x \to a} \bigl(f(x) - f(a)\bigr) = f'(a)\cdot 0 = 0 \implies \lim_{x \to a} f(x) = f(a) \]

Similarly, عندما differentiating an implicit relation \(F(x, y) = c\) بالنسبة إلى \(x\), \(y = y(x)\) is an inner الدالة of \(x\). By the Chain Rule, \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\bigl[y^n\bigr] = ny^{n-1}\dfrac{dy}{dx}\), and for product terms \(\dfrac{d}{dx}[xy] = y + x\dfrac{dy}{dx}\).

body.en:
Problem: Evaluate the limits: \[ (1) \; \lim_{x\to 3}\frac{x^2 - 9}{x - 3} \qquad (2) \; \lim_{x\to 0}\frac{\sqrt{x + 4} - 2}{x}. \]

Solution:

  1. Direct substitution gives \( \frac{0}{0} \). Factor numerator: \( x^2 - 9 = (x - 3)(x + 3) \). For \( x \neq 3 \): \[ \lim_{x\to 3}\frac{(x - 3)(x + 3)}{x - 3} = \lim_{x\to 3}(x + 3) = 3 + 3 = \mathbf{6}. \]
  2. Direct substitution gives \( \frac{0}{0} \). Rationalize the numerator by multiplying by the conjugate \( \sqrt{x + 4} + 2 \): \[ \lim_{x\to 0} \frac{(\sqrt{x + 4} - 2)(\sqrt{x + 4} + 2)}{x(\sqrt{x + 4} + 2)} = \lim_{x\to 0} \frac{(x + 4) - 4}{x(\sqrt{x + 4} + 2)} = \lim_{x\to 0} \frac{x}{x(\sqrt{x + 4} + 2)}. \] For \( x \neq 0 \), cancel \( x \): \[ \lim_{x\to 0} \frac{1}{\sqrt{x + 4} + 2} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{4} + 2} = \mathbf{\frac{1}{4}}. \]

body.en:
Problem (Medium): Consider the function \(f(x)\) whose graph is given below. The function is defined piecewise. For \(x \le 2\), \(f(x) = ax+b\). For \(x > 2\), \(f(x) = cx+d\). The graph of \(f(x)\) passes through the point \((0, 3)\). The limit of \(f(x)\) as \(x\) approaches 2 exists. Find the value of \(a\).

Step-by-Step Solution: For the limit of \(f(x)\) as \(x\) approaches 2 to exist, the left-hand limit must equal the right-hand limit. That is, \(\lim_{x \to 2^-} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 2^+} f(x)\). For \(x \le 2\), \(f(x) = ax+b\). So, the left-hand limit is \(\lim_{x \to 2^-} (ax+b) = 2a+b\). For \(x > 2\), \(f(x) = cx+d\). So, the right-hand limit is \(\lim_{x \to 2^+} (cx+d) = 2c+d\). Therefore, \(2a+b = 2c+d\). From the graph, we can see that the function passes through \((0, 3)\). This means \(f(0) = 3\). Since \(0 \le 2\), we use the definition \(f(x) = ax+b\). Thus, \(a(0)+b = 3\), which implies \(b = 3\). Also from the graph, we can see the point \((2, 1)\) is on the graph. Since \(2 \le 2\), \(f(2) = a(2)+b = 2a+b = 1\). Substituting \(b=3\), we get \(2a+3 = 1\), so \(2a = -2\), which means \(a = -1\). We also observe from the graph that the line segment for \(x>2\) passes through \((2, 1)\) and \((4, 0)\). This means \(f(x)=cx+d\) must satisfy these points. For \((2, 1)\): \(2c+d = 1\). For \((4, 0)\): \(4c+d = 0\). Subtracting the first equation from the second: \((4c+d) - (2c+d) = 0 - 1\), which gives \(2c = -1\), so \(c = -1/2\). Substituting \(c = -1/2\) into \(4c+d=0\): \(4(-1/2)+d = 0\), so \(-2+d=0\), which means \(d=2\). Now, let's check the limit condition: \(2a+b = 2c+d\). We found \(a=-1\), \(b=3\), \(c=-1/2\), \(d=2\). So, \(2(-1)+3 = -2+3 = 1\). And \(2(-1/2)+2 = -1+2 = 1\). The condition is satisfied. The question asks for the value of \(a\), which we found to be \(-1\). Common algebraic traps to avoid: 1. Mistaking the point \((2,1)\) as the endpoint of the \(cx+d\) segment, which would lead to using \(2c+d=1\) for the limit and potentially solving for \(c\) and \(d\) incorrectly. 2. Assuming continuity at \(x=2\) and not just the existence of the limit. While the graph *appears* continuous, the problem only states the limit exists.

So, the right-hand النهاية is \(\lim_{x \to 2^+} (cx+d) = 2c+d\). وبالتالي, \(2a+b = 2c+d\). From the التمثيل البياني, we can see that the الدالة passes through \((0, 3)\). This means \(f(0) = 3\). Since \(2 \le 2\), \(f(2) = a(2)+b = 2a+b = 1\). Substituting \(b=3\), we get \(2a+3 = 1\), so \(2a = -2\), which means \(a = -1\). We also observe from the التمثيل البياني that the line segment for \(x>2\) passes through \((2, 1)\) and \((4, 0)\). This means \(f(x)=cx+d\) must satisfy these points. For \((2, 1)\): \(2c+d = 1\). For \((4, 0)\): \(4c+d = 0\). Subtracting the first المعادلة from the second: \((4c+d) - (2c+d) = 0 - 1\), which gives \(2c = -1\), so \(c = -1/2\). Substituting \(c = -1/2\) into \(4c+d=0\): \(4(-1/2)+d = 0\), so \(-2+d=0\), which means \(d=2\). Now, let's check the النهاية condition: \(2a+b = 2c+d\). We found \(a=-1\), \(b=3\), \(c=-1/2\), \(d=2\). So, \(2(-1)+3 = -2+3 = 1\). And \(2(-1/2)+2 = -1+2 = 1\). The condition is satisfied. The question asks for the value of \(a\), which we found to be \(-1\). Common algebraic traps to avoid: 1. Mistaking the point \((2,1)\) as the endpoint of the \(cx+d\) segment, which would lead to using \(2c+d=1\) for the النهاية and potentially solving for \(c\) and \(d\) incorrectly. 2. Assuming continuity at \(x=2\) and not just the existence of the النهاية. While the التمثيل البياني *appears* continuous, the problem only states the النهاية exists.

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

Evaluate the one-sided limit \( \displaystyle \lim_{x\to 2^-} \frac{|x - 2|}{x^2 - 4} \).
question.ar:
Level 1 · Foundations

احسب قيمة the one-sided limit \( \displaystyle \lim_{x\to 2^-} \frac{|x - 2|}{x^2 - 4} \).

solution.en: When \( x \to 2^- \), \( x < 2 \), so \( x - 2 < 0 \implies |x - 2| = -(x - 2) \). Factor the denominator: \( x^2 - 4 = (x - 2)(x + 2) \). Substitute: \[ \lim_{x\to 2^-} \frac{-(x - 2)}{(x - 2)(x + 2)} = \lim_{x\to 2^-} \frac{-1}{x + 2} = \frac{-1}{2 + 2} = \mathbf{-\frac{1}{4}}. \]

label.en: ● Rigorous \(\varepsilon - \delta\) Proofs · Linear and Quadratic Functions
label.ar: ● Rigorous \(\varepsilon - \delta\) Proofs · Linear and Quadratic الدوال

body.en:
1. Linear Limit: Prove that \(\lim_{x\to 3} (4x - 5) = 7\).

Proof: Let \(\varepsilon > 0\) be given. We want \(|(4x - 5) - 7| < \varepsilon \iff |4x - 12| < \varepsilon \iff 4|x - 3| < \varepsilon \iff |x - 3| < \frac{\varepsilon}{4}\). Choose \(\delta = \frac{\varepsilon}{4} > 0\). Assume \(0 < |x - 3| < \delta\). Then: \[ |(4x - 5) - 7| = 4|x - 3| < 4\delta = 4\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{4}\right) = \varepsilon. \quad \blacksquare \]

2. Quadratic Limit with Preliminary Bounding: Prove that \(\lim_{x\to 2} x^2 = 4\).

Proof: Let \(\varepsilon > 0\) be given. We have \(|x^2 - 4| = |x - 2| \cdot |x + 2|\). Constrain \(\delta \le 1\). If \(|x - 2| < 1\), then \(1 < x < 3 \implies 3 < x + 2 < 5 \implies |x + 2| < 5\). Thus \(|x^2 - 4| < 5|x - 2|\). To make this \(< \varepsilon\), set \(|x - 2| < \frac{\varepsilon}{5}\). Choose \(\delta = \min\left(1, \frac{\varepsilon}{5}\right)\). If \(0 < |x - 2| < \delta\), then \(|x - 2| < 1\) (so \(|x + 2| < 5\)) and \(|x - 2| < \frac{\varepsilon}{5}\). Hence: \[ |x^2 - 4| = |x - 2|\cdot|x + 2| < \left(\frac{\varepsilon}{5}\right)(5) = \varepsilon. \quad \blacksquare \]

label.en: ● Theorem & Geometric Proof · The Squeeze Theorem & Fundamental Trig Limits
label.ar: ● مبرهنة & Geometric برهان · The Squeeze مبرهنة & Fundamental Trig النهايات

body.en:
The Squeeze (Sandwich) Theorem: If \( g(x) \le f(x) \le h(x) \) for all \( x \) in an open interval containing \( c \) (except possibly at \( c \)), and \( \lim_{x\to c} g(x) = \lim_{x\to c} h(x) = L \), then \( \lim_{x\to c} f(x) = L \).

Proof of \( \lim_{\theta \to 0} \frac{\sin\theta}{\theta} = 1 \): Consider the unit circle with angle \( \theta \in (0, \pi/2) \). Construct: (1) interior triangle of area \( \frac{1}{2}\sin\theta \); (2) sector of area \( \frac{1}{2}\theta \); (3) exterior right triangle of area \( \frac{1}{2}\tan\theta \). Comparing areas: \[ \frac{1}{2}\sin\theta < \frac{1}{2}\theta < \frac{1}{2}\tan\theta. \] Divide by \( \frac{1}{2}\sin\theta > 0 \): \[ 1 < \frac{\theta}{\sin\theta} < \frac{1}{\cos\theta}. \] Taking reciprocals reverses inequalities: \[ \cos\theta < \frac{\sin\theta}{\theta} < 1. \] Since \( \cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta \) and \( \frac{\sin(-\theta)}{-\theta} = \frac{\sin\theta}{\theta} \), this holds for all \( \theta \neq 0 \) near 0. Because \( \lim_{\theta\to 0} \cos\theta = 1 \) and \( \lim_{\theta\to 0} 1 = 1 \), by the Squeeze Theorem: \[ \lim_{\theta \to 0} \frac{\sin\theta}{\theta} = \mathbf{1}. \quad \blacksquare \]

label.ar: Level 2 (Medium) — مثال محلول · Trigonometric النهايات & المعامل Continuity

body.en:
Problem: Determine constants \( a \) and \( b \) such that the function \( f \) is continuous everywhere: \[ f(x) = egin{cases} \dfrac{\sin(ax)}{x}, & x < 0 \ b + 2, & x = 0 \ \dfrac{x^2 - 4x + 3}{x - 3} + 5, & x > 0 \; (x eq 3) \ a + b, & x = 3. \end{cases} \]

Step 1 · Continuity at \( x = 0 \):
• Left-hand limit: \( \lim_{x o 0^-} rac{\sin(ax)}{x} = \lim_{x o 0^-} a \left( rac{\sin(ax)}{ax} ight) = a(1) = a \).
• Right-hand limit: \( \lim_{x o 0^+} \left( rac{x^2 - 4x + 3}{x - 3} + 5 ight) = rac{3}{-3} + 5 = -1 + 5 = 4 \).
• Value at 0: \( f(0) = b + 2 \).
For continuity at \( x = 0 \), all three must match: \( a = 4 \) and \( b + 2 = 4 \implies b = 2 \).

Step 2 · Check Continuity at \( x = 3 \):
• For \( x eq 3 \), \( rac{x^2 - 4x + 3}{x - 3} + 5 = rac{(x - 3)(x - 1)}{x - 3} + 5 = (x - 1) + 5 = x + 4 \).
• Limit as \( x o 3 \): \( \lim_{x o 3} (x + 4) = 3 + 4 = 7 \).
• Value at 3: \( f(3) = a + b = 4 + 2 = 6 eq 7 \).
Notice \( f(3) = a + b = 6 eq 7 \). Therefore, setting \( a = 4 \) and \( b = 2 \) secures continuity at \( x = 0 \); to make \( f \) continuous everywhere on \( \mathbb{R} \), we must redefine the point at \( x = 3 \) to equal 7.

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

Evaluate the trigonometric limit: \[ \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{1 - \cos(3x)}{x^2}. \]
question.ar:
Level 2 · Medium

احسب قيمة the trigonometric limit: \[ \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{1 - \cos(3x)}{x^2}. \]

solution.en: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate \( 1 + \cos(3x) \): \[ \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{(1 - \cos(3x))(1 + \cos(3x))}{x^2(1 + \cos(3x))} = \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{1 - \cos^2(3x)}{x^2(1 + \cos(3x))} = \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\sin^2(3x)}{x^2(1 + \cos(3x))}. \] Re-group terms to leverage \( \lim_{u\to 0}\frac{\sin u}{u} = 1 \): \[ = \lim_{x \to 0} \left[ \left(\frac{\sin(3x)}{3x}\right)^2 \cdot 3^2 \cdot \frac{1}{1 + \cos(3x)} \right]. \] Evaluating individual limits: \[ = (1)^2 \cdot 9 \cdot \frac{1}{1 + \cos(0)} = 9 \cdot \frac{1}{1 + 1} = \mathbf{\frac{9}{2}}. \]

label.en: ● Precise Definitions of Limits at Infinity & Infinite Limits (with Proofs)
label.ar: ● Precise Definitions of النهايات at Infinity & Infinite النهايات (with Proofs)

body.en:
1. Limit at Infinity: \(\displaystyle\lim_{x\to \infty} f(x) = L\) means: \[ \forall \varepsilon > 0, \; \exists M > 0 \; \text{such that} \; x > M \implies |f(x) - L| < \varepsilon. \]

Proof: Prove that \(\lim_{x\to\infty} \frac{2x+1}{x+3} = 2\). Let \(\varepsilon > 0\) be given. For \(x > 0\): \[ \left|\frac{2x+1}{x+3} - 2\right| = \left|\frac{2x+1 - 2x - 6}{x+3}\right| = \frac{5}{x+3}. \] Setting \(\frac{5}{x+3} < \varepsilon \iff x+3 > \frac{5}{\varepsilon} \iff x > \frac{5}{\varepsilon} - 3\). Choose \(M = \max\left(1, \frac{5}{\varepsilon} - 3\right)\). For any \(x > M\): \[ \left|\frac{2x+1}{x+3} - 2\right| = \frac{5}{x+3} < \frac{5}{M+3} \le \frac{5}{(5/\varepsilon)} = \varepsilon. \quad \blacksquare \]

2. Infinite Limit at a Point: \(\displaystyle\lim_{x\to c} f(x) = \infty\) means: \[ \forall M > 0, \; \exists \delta > 0 \; \text{such that} \; 0 < |x - c| < \delta \implies f(x) > M. \]

Proof: Prove that \(\lim_{x\to 0} \frac{1}{x^2} = \infty\). Let \(M > 0\) be given arbitrary. Choose \(\delta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{M}} > 0\). Assume \(0 < |x - 0| < \delta\). Then \(|x| < \frac{1}{\sqrt{M}} \implies x^2 < \frac{1}{M}\). Taking reciprocals gives: \[ \frac{1}{x^2} > M. \quad \blacksquare \]

label.en: ● Theorem & Analytical Application · The Intermediate Value Theorem (IVT)
label.ar: ● مبرهنة & Analytical Application · The Intermediate Value مبرهنة (IVT)

body.en:
Theorem (IVT): Let \( f \) be continuous on the closed interval \( [a, b] \). If \( d \) is any real number strictly between \( f(a) \) and \( f(b) \) (so either \( f(a) < d < f(b) \) or \( f(b) < d < f(a) \)), then there exists at least one number \( c \in (a, b) \) such that: \[ f(c) = d. \]

Bolzano's Corollary (Root Existence): If \( f \) is continuous on \( [a, b] \) and \( f(a) \) and \( f(b) \) possess opposite signs (i.e. \( f(a) \cdot f(b) < 0 \)), then there exists at least one real zero \( c \in (a, b) \) such that \( f(c) = 0 \).

label.en: Level 3 (Advanced) — Worked Example · Rigorous IVT Root Isolation & End Behavior
label.ar: Level 3 (Advanced) — مثال محلول · Rigorous IVT Root Isolation & End Behavior

body.en:
Problem: Prove rigorously that the transcendental equation \( e^{-x} = x^2 - 2 \) has at least one real root in the interval \( (1, 2) \).

Step 1 · Construct the Continuity Test Function: Define \( g(x) = e^{-x} - x^2 + 2 \). Because \( e^{-x} \) is exponential and \( -x^2 + 2 \) is polynomial, \( g \) is continuous everywhere on \( \mathbb{R} \), and specifically continuous on the closed interval \( [1, 2] \).

Step 2 · Evaluate Interval Endpoints:
• At \( x = 1 \): \( g(1) = e^{-1} - 1^2 + 2 = \frac{1}{e} + 1 \approx 0.368 + 1 = 1.368 > 0 \).
• At \( x = 2 \): \( g(2) = e^{-2} - 2^2 + 2 = \frac{1}{e^2} - 2 \approx 0.135 - 2 = -1.865 < 0 \).

Step 3 · Invoke the Intermediate Value Theorem:
Since \( g \) is continuous on \( [1, 2] \), and \( 0 \) lies strictly between \( g(2) < 0 \) and \( g(1) > 0 \), by the Intermediate Value Theorem there exists at least one value \( c \in (1, 2) \) such that: \[ g(c) = 0 \implies e^{-c} - c^2 + 2 = 0 \implies e^{-c} = c^2 - 2. \quad \blacksquare \]

Since \( g \) is continuous on \( [1, 2] \), and \( 0 \) lies strictly between \( g(2) < 0 \) and \( g(1) > 0 \), by the Intermediate Value مبرهنة there exists at least one value \( c \in (1, 2) \) such that: \[ g(c) = 0 \implies e^{-c} - c^2 + 2 = 0 \implies e^{-c} = c^2 - 2. \quad \blacksquare \]

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced

Evaluate the limit analytically without using L'Hôpital's Rule: \[ \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\sqrt{1 + \tan x} - \sqrt{1 + \sin x}}{x^3}. \]
question.ar:
Level 3 · Advanced

احسب قيمة النهاية analytically without using L'Hôpital's Rule: \[ \lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\sqrt{1 + \tan x} - \sqrt{1 + \sin x}}{x^3}. \]

solution.en:
Step 1 · Rationalize the Numerator: Multiply by \( \sqrt{1 + \tan x} + \sqrt{1 + \sin x} \): \[ \lim_{x\to 0} \frac{(1 + \tan x) - (1 + \sin x)}{x^3(\sqrt{1 + \tan x} + \sqrt{1 + \sin x})} = \lim_{x\to 0} \frac{\tan x - \sin x}{x^3(\sqrt{1 + \tan x} + \sqrt{1 + \sin x})}. \]

Step 2 · Factor Trigonometric Terms: \[ \tan x - \sin x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x} - \sin x = \sin x\left(\frac{1 - \cos x}{\cos x}\right). \] Multiply numerator and denominator by \( 1 + \cos x \): \[ = \sin x \cdot \frac{1 - \cos^2 x}{\cos x(1 + \cos x)} = \frac{\sin^3 x}{\cos x(1 + \cos x)}. \]

Step 3 · Decompose Limit: \[ = \lim_{x\to 0} \left[ \left(\frac{\sin x}{x}\right)^3 \cdot \frac{1}{\cos x(1 + \cos x)} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 + \tan x} + \sqrt{1 + \sin x}} \right]. \] As \( x \to 0 \):
• \( \left(\frac{\sin x}{x}\right)^3 \to 1^3 = 1 \)
• \( \frac{1}{\cos(0)(1 + \cos 0)} = \frac{1}{1(1 + 1)} = \frac{1}{2} \)
• \( \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 + 0} + \sqrt{1 + 0}} = \frac{1}{1 + 1} = \frac{1}{2} \).
Multiplying: \[ = 1 \cdot \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{2} = \mathbf{\frac{1}{4}}. \]

body.en:
Indeterminate Form 0/0: Obtaining \(\frac{0}{0}\) from direct substitution does NOT mean the limit is 0, 1, or does not exist. It is an indeterminate form signaling that an algebraic simplification (factoring, conjugate rationalization, trig identity, or L'Hôpital's Rule) must be performed.

Two-Sided Limit Existence: The overall limit \(\lim_{x\to c} f(x) = L\) exists IF AND ONLY IF both one-sided limits exist and agree: \(\lim_{x\to c^-} f(x) = \lim_{x\to c^+} f(x) = L\). For piece-wise and absolute value functions, always verify both directions separately.

Continuity Checklist: A function \(f\) is continuous at \(x = c\) only if all 3 conditions hold: (1) \(f(c)\) is defined; (2) \(\lim_{x\to c} f(x)\) exists; (3) \(\lim_{x\to c} f(x) = f(c)\). A graph with a hole where the limit exists is STILL discontinuous.

IVT Preconditions: Never invoke the Intermediate Value Theorem without explicitly stating that \(f\) is continuous on the closed interval \([a, b]\). Missing this continuity justification loses full points on college exams.

body.en:
Every algebraic and elementary transcendental model is built by transforming one of the nine core parent functions via \(g(x) = a\,f(x - h) + k\), where \(|a|\) scales vertically (reflecting across the \(x\)-axis if \(a < 0\)), \(h\) shifts horizontally, and \(k\) shifts vertically:

Quadratic\(a(x - h)^2 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)Parabola vertex \((h, k)\), axis \(x = h\)
Cubic\(a(x - h)^3 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Inflection center \((h, k)\), S-curve
